name: LucidPro 50K · $1,200 daily limit
source: Account holder, 2026-09-27, pasted LucidPro 50K's rule table: account size $50,000; profit target $3,000; max loss limit $2,000; daily loss limit $1,200; max size 4 minis or 40 micros -- and said the daily loss limit can be removed as an option. Asked what hitting the daily limit does: it STOPS YOU FOR THE DAY (soft), the account survives. Earlier the same day: no consistency rule and no minimum days. Still INHERITED FROM FLEX and NOT confirmed for LucidPro: the lock (+$2,100 -> +$100 floor), the max loss being EOD-trailing, payout terms, scaling and session rules. CONFIRMED IN FULL by the account holder later on 2026-09-27 ("yes im confirming the lucid pro"), after being told the lock, EOD trailing and payout terms were copied from Flex: every number in this file is now the account holder's.
payout_ladder: first cheques capped $2,000, later $2,500; up to 5 payouts then live review; 90/10 split beyond
notes: Contract scaling (funded): start 20 micros, 30 at +$1,000, 40 at +$2,000; 4 minis = 40 micros is the hard cap (eval too). NOT enforced by the simulator — surfaced as a warning when a ledger exceeds it.
Flat by 16:10 ET, no overnight holds. NOT enforced by the simulator — surfaced as a warning.
Only the FIRST payout is simulated; the ladder above is informational.
Trailing max loss is measured END OF DAY, not intraday: the floor moves up with EOD peak profit and never moves down.
The floor LOCKS at +$100 once EOD profit reaches +$2,100 — from then on the account cannot be trailed below +$100.
NO consistency rule and NO minimum trading days (account holder, 2026-09-27): `consistency: null` disables the check, `eval_min_days: 1` means a single day that reaches +$3,000 passes.
Payout requires 5 separate days >= $150 AND net > 0. Payout amount is 50% of profit capped at $2,000, so the max payout additionally needs >= $4,000 profit.

SOFT daily loss limit $1,200: the moment the day's P&L (closed trades plus the open one) reaches -$1,200 you are closed out at -$1,200 and stopped for the day; the account survives. The tester applies it per trade using each trade's tick-level worst moment (MAE), so a trade that dipped past -$1,200 and then won is correctly counted as stopped out. Applied to the eval, the funded account and the Monte Carlo ruin walk. Small approximations: the stop fills at exactly -$1,200, and overlapping positions are walked one after the other.
Confirmed in full by the account holder 2026-09-27, including the terms that match Flex (lock +$2,100 -> +$100 floor, EOD trailing, payout terms, scaling, 16:10 flat).
disclaimer: Account-holder snapshot 2026-09-27 — verify against LucidPro's current rulebook if Lucid changes its terms.
